value: Bounded hosted-commercial-model spot check (NOT a matched replication of the 200-case local downstream runs)

Addresses the paper's Limitations note that no hosted commercial API was tested; the owner has no usable API key, so the hosted 'model' here is a Claude model reached through the Claude Code agent harness, acting as the downstream agent for a bounded sample of PrivacyLens cases.

The downstream-agent completions were produced by a Claude model inside an interactive Claude Code agent session (human-in-the-loop style: each rendered prompt was read and answered in turn within this session), NOT by a scripted, batched call to the Anthropic Messages API. This is a materially different regime from the local open-weight runs, which called Ollama programmatically in a loop with fixed decoding settings.
claude-code-harness-hosted (a descriptive placeholder, not an API model string)

The harness's own system context identifies the running model as 'Sonnet 5' (model id 'claude-sonnet-5'). This is the harness's self-report, not something independently verified from a raw API response (no response header, system-fingerprint, or dated snapshot suffix such as the 'claude-*-YYYYMMDD' form that Anthropic API responses normally carry was observed, because no direct API call was made). We report this label as given and do not upgrade it to a verified, dated model version string.

NOT controllable and NOT recorded: no temperature, top_p, or seed could be set or logged for harness-mediated completions, unlike the local runs (temperature 0, top_p 1, seed 17). Any single-run comparison to the local numbers is therefore not decoding-matched.

NOT RUN. No PrivacyLens Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 judge call was made (no local judge model server was used for this CPU-only, no-GPU check), so leak_any, leak_count, and helpfulness are left blank in the rows file. Only exact-identifier exposure (ids_in_final_action / ids_total), which is computed by deterministic code rather than a judge model, was scored.

no_protection ONLY. See 'conditions_not_covered' for why placeholder:learned_lr and symbolic_late (requested as additional conditions) were not attempted.

The released (mediated) instruction/trajectory text that privacylens_downstream_suite.py actually shows the agent under placeholder:*, casper_style, symbolic_*, llm_sanitizer:*, and abstraction:* conditions is not persisted anywhere in this repository: ROW_FIELDS in privacylens_downstream_suite.py stores only aggregate counts (ids_in_output, tokens_in_output, etc.), and the per-model response cache in ollama_cache/*.jsonl is keyed by a SHA-256 hash of the full request (model+messages+options), which is not reversible to the plaintext prompt. Reconstructing those conditions' released text today would require re-running the current presidio/spacy/gliner/learned_lr detector stack, which is exactly the substitution this check was told not to make, since a detector version difference would silently change what is being compared against the recorded runs. no_protection is the sole exception: its 'release' step is the identity function (Condition.apply returns instr, traj unchanged), so the exact text the recorded local-model runs saw is fully and losslessly reconstructable from the already-committed external_data/privacylens/main_data.json and agent_prompts_naive.jsonl -- no detector involved, no version drift possible.

To make a mediated condition (e.g. placeholder:learned_lr) replayable without re-deriving it from a live detector stack, privacylens_downstream_suite.py's ROW_FIELDS (and the write in evaluate_case, around the 'instr_r, traj_r, mapping, mode = cond.apply(...)' line) would need to persist the released instruction/trajectory text itself -- e.g. an added released_instruction/released_trajectory column in the rows CSV, or a separate per-case sidecar file written at generation time -- for every future run. No such field exists today in any recorded run's output.

The 200-case pool used by the recorded qwen3-32B and llama3.3-70B no_protection runs was reconstructed as random.Random(17).sample(cases, 200) over the 493 cases in external_data/privacylens/main_data.json (same code path as privacylens_downstream_suite.py's --sample-seed default) and verified to match exactly (case-name set equality) against the case column of the recorded rows files.

The hosted 40-case point estimate (12.7%) falls within both local 200-case models' 95% bootstrap CIs. With n=40 the hosted estimate has no comparably tight CI of its own and should be read as directionally consistent with, not a precise match to, the local no_protection numbers -- and the two runs are not decoding-matched (see decoding_parameters).

This is a bounded, honest hosted-model spot check intended as an internal robustness signal, not a matched replication of the paper's 200-case local evaluation: single condition (no_protection only), n=40 vs n=200, no judge-based leak-rate or helpfulness scoring, uncontrolled decoding, and human-in-the-loop harness completions rather than a scripted API loop.
